about: Questions asked of the planner. Each answer should spawn new questions; `unlocks` names the data that would answer an open one.

questions.question: Where should a new GP surgery go?
questions.finding: Corrected 28 Oct 2026 with official NHS practices (gps.json): by walking distance, St Peters near Hidcote Close (WR5 3; ~3,900 households brought within 15 min). The earlier Norton Road answer used OpenStreetMap GPs, which missed surgeries and counted hospital clinics.

questions.question: Does being far from a GP actually harm people's health?
questions.finding: Corrected 28 Oct 2026 with official NHS practices (gps.json): still no sign. After age and deprivation, GP walking distance shows no link with Census 2021 bad health (t = 0.8). Deprivation explains most of the difference.

questions.question: Can people actually get an appointment? Which surgeries are over capacity?
questions.unlocks: NHS Digital: patients registered per GP practice, GP workforce (FTE GPs per practice)
questions.finding: Partly, without GP staff numbers (not published where we can reach it). 9 practices serve Worcester, all large (6,900–21,900 patients; England's typical practice ~8,800). Patients finding the wait acceptable (GP Patient Survey 2024, England 66%): Haresfield House 55%, St Martin's Gate 58%, St Johns House 59%, up to Spring Gardens 84%. Pressure by geography (residents whose nearest surgery it is, vs its registered list): Elbury Moor 31,700 vs 12,400; Spring Gardens 27,300 vs 20,100; St Johns House 19,900 vs 13,800.

questions.question: Why is health worst around Selsey Close and Windermere Drive, when a GP is 12–18 min away?
questions.unlocks: Index of Multiple Deprivation (income, employment, housing), access to green space, fast-food density, air quality

questions.question: Do older people in Lower Wick (35% over 65, 38 min walk to a GP) have a bus or car to get there?
questions.unlocks: Census 2021 car availability (TS045); bus timetables (Bus Open Data) for real public-transport times
questions.finding: Corrected 28 Oct 2026 with official NHS practices (gps.json): Lower Wick (012E) is 27 min from a GP on foot, ~25 by bus or walking. 15% of households have no car; only 11% have a frequent bus stop within 5 min.

questions.question: Should 'best site' be ranked by need (health, age, deprivation) instead of just households within walking distance?
questions.unlocks: A need score per neighbourhood from data already loaded; change rankChanges to weight by need
questions.finding: Corrected 28 Oct 2026 with official NHS practices (gps.json): ranking by need still moves the answer: the top need-weighted GP sites are Bath Road and Nunnery Lane in St Peters, and Winchcombe Drive in the Warndon Villages. (Before the correction it pointed to Malvern Road, St John's, but Severn Valley Medical Practice, the town's largest, is already there.)

questions.question: How often do buses actually run from Lower Wick to a GP surgery?
questions.unlocks: Bus Open Data GTFS timetables (West Midlands, 207 MB, reachable): trips per hour and journey times to each surgery
questions.finding: Corrected 28 Oct 2026 with official NHS practices (gps.json): buses help a little. Lower Wick: GP 27 min walking, ~25 by bus or walking; only 11% near a frequent stop. Town-wide, buses cut the average GP trip from 22 to 18 min; 54% of households have a stop with 4+ buses an hour within 5 min.

questions.question: Is the west side (St John's, Dines Green, Lower Wick) cut off by the River Severn, with too few crossings?
questions.unlocks: Detour ratios already computed (access.js) split by river side; count of walkable and drivable crossings; traffic counts on the crossings
questions.finding: Corrected 28 Oct 2026 with official NHS practices (gps.json): the river matters less than it first looked. West bank 26 min to a GP on average, east bank 20.5 (earlier 31 vs 16 came from missing west-bank surgeries and hospital clinics counted as GPs on the east). 6 walkable crossings, 2 for cars; the best new footbridge saves under a minute per household.

questions.question: Why do corner shops seem to do better in poorer neighbourhoods, and the opposite in well-off ones?
questions.finding: Partly true, weakly. The most deprived third of Worcester's neighbourhoods has ~1.7x the convenience shops per household (0.96 vs 0.58 per 1,000) and 2x the supermarkets. The likelier driver is car ownership, not money as such: 33% of households there have no car vs 11% in the least deprived third. Only 30 convenience shops are mapped in OSM, so treat as a hint.

questions.question: Are corner shops thriving or just surviving, and what else (takeaways, cafes, pubs) clusters with deprivation and bad health?
questions.unlocks: Food Standards Agency hygiene ratings API (reachable): every food business with type and location; opening and closing dates over time
questions.finding: Food Standards Agency register (546 food businesses in Worcester; 111 small food shops vs 30 in OpenStreetMap). Leaving out the 2 city-centre neighbourhoods: small food shops are ~3.5x as common in the most deprived third (2.37 vs 0.67 per 1,000 households), and track households without a car (r = 0.36) a little more than deprivation (0.32). Takeaways show no link with deprivation (r = 0.02) or bad health (-0.03) in Worcester, against the usual assumption. Whether shops are thriving or just surviving needs openings and closures over time.

questions.question: What should happen to County Hall, Worcester?
questions.unlocks: Site size and condition; planning.data.gov.uk (local plan, constraints, listed status); access scores for the site as homes vs offices vs a health hub; traffic on Spetchley Road; Worcestershire County Council's own estate plans
questions.progress: Scenarios (scenarios/*.json, scored by `npm run planner -- scenarios`): a health hub at County Hall lifts the town score +0.8 and cuts the average GP walk by 1.2 min. 600 homes alone (an illustrative number) would leave the new residents ~30 min from a GP (shop 7, school 10.5); homes + hub fixes that (+1.2 overall). But a surgery at Bath Road, St Peters, does more for existing residents (+1.7; GP walk -2.8 min, need-weighted -1.7). Still open: site size and condition, the council's plans, traffic on Spetchley Road. Who gains: a County Hall hub saves 6,620 households ~10 min to a GP (607 without a car); a Bath Road surgery saves 7,877 households ~19 min (744 without a car).

questions.question: What should we do with Worcester's empty shops?
questions.unlocks: Where they are: OSM vacant/disused shop tags (patchy), FSA closures, Valuation Office business rates list, council vacancy surveys; footfall proxies (bus stops, car parks, traffic counts); what similar towns did
questions.progress: 35 empty shops are mapped in OpenStreetMap (a lower bound; volunteers record them unevenly): ~27 in the city centre around High Street, Foregate Street and Crowngate, including the former Debenhams and Ernest Jones (checked Aug 2025); Carpetright at Blackpole; and a former Costcutter on Ambleside Drive, Warndon. Shown as grey dots. Still open: an official vacancy count (business rates / council surveys) and what each unit could become, tested as scenarios.

questions.question: What would a 'New Worcester' look like, cyclist-friendly vs driver-friendly?
questions.unlocks: Scenarios as sets of network edits, scored on one dashboard (access, traffic, cycling, health benefit via WHO HEAT, safety via STATS19). Ties together q7, q8, q11, q12
questions.progress: Scenario tool built: a scenario is a named set of changes (new places, homes, roads) scored on one scorecard against Worcester today (access score, share within targets, walk and bus-or-walk minutes, need-weighted GP walk, and the new homes' own access). First four scenarios are about County Hall and St Peters. Cycling and car-free changes need a mode-choice model next.

questions.question: Could a west-bank health hub work at or near Malvern Road, St John's: is there a building or site, and do buses reach it?
questions.unlocks: planning.data.gov.uk brownfield land and sites; empty commercial buildings in St John's (links to q12); Bus Open Data timetables from Lower Wick, Dines Green and Henwick (links to q7); NHS practice list sizes for the existing west-bank surgeries (links to q3)
questions.progress: Location checks out on access: a GP at Malvern Road cuts Lower Wick (012E) from 38 to ~16 min walking and the west bank's average from 31 to 24 min. Still open: a building or site, and capacity of the existing west-bank surgeries.
questions.finding: Withdrawn: it rested on OpenStreetMap missing Severn Valley Medical Practice (21,893 patients), which already sits in St John's.

questions.question: Which neighbourhoods have the worst bus service for their need (old, no car, deprived) and where would one more frequent route help most?
questions.unlocks: bus.json (frequency per stop, bus-or-walk minutes per neighbourhood) + need score already loaded; route shapes from the GTFS shapes.txt to test a rerouted or extra service

questions.question: Is St Peters really without a GP within reach (41 min walk around Foxglove Road), or do branch surgeries fill the gap?
questions.unlocks: Branch surgery sites (NHS ODS branch codes, practice websites); where St Peters residents are actually registered (practice-to-LSOA registration counts, NHS Digital)

questions.question: Why is Elbury Moor the nearest surgery for ~31,700 people but registers 12,400? Where do Warndon's residents actually go?
questions.unlocks: Patients registered by LSOA per practice (NHS Digital, blocked from this cloud box: needs another route or a local run)

questions.question: Are Worcester's corner shops opening or closing, and does losing one hurt households without a car?
questions.unlocks: FSA register snapshots over time (new and removed businesses), Companies House dissolutions, OSM disused:shop tags; a scenario that removes a shop and scores the households without a car around it
questions.finding: For the one closed corner shop mapped (former Costcutter, Ambleside Drive, Warndon: the worst-health neighbourhood, half of households without a car), reopening it brings 289 households a shop an average 1.4 min closer, 71 of them without a car. Other small shops nearby cover most of the loss by distance; price and range may matter more and aren't in this data. Openings and closures over time still need FSA snapshots.
